fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) - National central bank of the French Republic; monetary policy and foreign exchange reserve functions are exercised within the European System of Central Banks under the authority of the European Central Bank; prudential supervision of credit institutions and payment institutions is delegated to the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR), an institution attached to Banque de France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is an EU Member State and a euro-area member, and the euro is fully convertible. Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union guarantees free movement of capital and transfers between Member States and third countries, subject only to non-discriminatory public-policy derogations and EU financial sanctions. France abolished its prior authorisation exchange-control system on 29 December 1989 and has not reinstated administrative FX controls. Both capital-account and current-account transactions are free of any licensing requirement, and profit remittances by a French SARL to its non-resident shareholders are freely payable without any currency conversion gate. Residual obligations are statistical and documentary only: all cross-border financial flows must be capable of transparent identification through the Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting framework, and all payments must be screened against EU, UN, OFAC and French national financial sanctions lists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France operates no mandatory export-proceeds surrender regime. Export receipts derived from the distribution of commercial aircraft rotables and avionics surplus may be retained indefinitely in USD or any other freely convertible currency, converted into EUR, or applied directly to permitted FX hedging instruments. The sole compulsory layer is statistical reporting to Banque de France: a French resident company whose cross-border financial transactions exceed the regulatory aggregate threshold of EUR 1,000,000 over twelve consecutive months must file the monthly Liaison Financière (balance-of-payments declaration) through its resident bank or the Banque de France direct collection channel. In addition, all export movements of goods must be reflected in the customs declaration of exchanges of goods (Déclaration d'Échanges de Biens) submitted through the DELTA system. There is no conversion ratio, no mandatory conversion timeline and no certificate of validation of the receipt of export proceeds; exporters may maintain foreign-currency accounts indefinitely and repatriate funds at their own commercial discretion.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH as a complementary payment rail; LOW-MEDIUM as the primary escrow vehicle. ACPR-licensed electronic money institutions and payment institutions (e.g., Treezor, Mangopay, Lemonway, Qonto, Lydia/Sumeria) can legally open multi-currency IBANs and execute SWIFT MT103 transfers through partner banks under the PSD2 e-money passport. However, an EMI is prohibited from granting credit, issuing bank guarantees, or opening documentary credits, all of which are core instruments in the aviation surplus spare-parts escrow and settlement cycle. Additionally, the e-money safeguarding obligation under Article L525-4 of the French Monetary and Financial Code means that funds held by an EMI are not held as a classic bank deposit and do not legally constitute a true escrow account. Most institutional aviation counterparties and escrow instruction letters therefore require a full credit institution (bank) rather than an EMI as the escrow agent. EMIs remain workable for low-value disbursements, contractor payments and quick vendor settlements, but the main inbound aviation escrow and trade-finance accounts should be established with a Tier-1 French commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one statutory manager (gérant) or the ultimate beneficial owner is in practice mandatory for the activation of a capital escrow account and trade-finance facilities in the French domestic banking market. Although French AML/CFT law, notably Article R561-5 of the French Monetary and Financial Code, nominally permits fully remote digital onboarding through secure video identification and eIDAS-qualified electronic signatures, French banks impose, as a matter of internal risk policy, an in-person interview at the corporate banking centre for medium-risk aviation trading structures, particularly where the SARL has non-resident shareholders and expects large escrow wire volumes. Directors should therefore plan one structured in-person KYC meeting at the selected bank's headquarters in Paris (most likely for BNP Paribas, Société Générale or CACIB). Fully remote opening without any physical visit is unlikely to succeed for the capital escrow account, although the operational EUR account may subsequently be administered digitally after the face-to-face validation is completed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Structurally opaque non-resident shareholding chain where the French SARL is wholly owned by a foreign parent located in a non-EEA jurisdiction, especially with intermediate holding entities and no clear natural-person ultimate beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate organisation chart reaching every natural-person UBO; certified copies of passports and proof of residential address for all UBOs; the French SARL's registration extract from the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) together with the filed Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (EDB); certified copy of the immediate parent's statutory registers or equivalent beneficial-ownership filing; audited financial statements for the parent and intermediate companies covering the last three fiscal years; sworn written attestation of the legal source and origin of the injected capital funds; certified resolutions or powers of attorney authorising the gérant to open accounts; and a French legal opinion confirming the real substance of the group and the absence of any shell-structure indicators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aviation surplus provenance risk, including potential yellow-tag and bogus or cancelled EASA/FAA release certificates, undocumented rotables, or parts sourced from distressed airlines whose maintenance records cannot be verified - perceived fraud typology of certified rotables trade.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full serialisation and traceability audit file comprising EASA Form 1 (F1) certificates or FAA 8130-3 dual release tags for every high-value rotable purchased; AS9120 and/or ISO 9001 quality certification of each major upstream supplier; the signed purchase and distribution agreements with complete chain-of-custody documentation by aircraft tail number and component part number; independent technical appraisal or airworthiness inspection report from an accredited aviation consultancy; photographs and customs export forms evidencing physical movement of goods; and a written compliance policy demonstrating procedures to detect counterfeit, unapproved and suspect unapproved parts (CUSP).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction velocity in escrow accounts, particularly rapid inbound wires from a newly formed SARL followed by near-simultaneous outbound disbursement to foreign MRO shops or teardown facilities in jurisdictions carrying a higher money-laundering risk profile - circular or 'flight' capital typology.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed 12-month business plan and projected cash-flow model consistent with the escrow inflows; commercial dossier for each underlying transaction including purchase orders, invoices, delivery notes and polling repurchase agreements; signed escrow instruction letter specifying the release conditions to the French bank; complete due-diligence reports and sanctions-screen printouts (EU, OFAC, UN) for each counterparty payment beneficiary; UETR-coded SWIFT records and the SARL's internal transaction monitoring and reconciliation policy; and third-party confirmation from the aircraft lessor, airline or regulated aviation broker that generated the surplus inventory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and dual-use exposure in the aviation sector, including suspicion of diversion of parts to military end-users, Russian/Iranian air freight operators, or embargoed destination countries - a mandatory red flag even when total transaction amounts are low.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified export-compliance programme including written internal procedures aligned to EU Dual-Use Regulation 2021/821; EU/OFAC sanctions and restricted-party screening certificates covering all route counterparties and beneficial owners; completed end-user and end-use undertakings for each commercial sale; concluded customs export declarations via the DELTA/DELTA-G system (Déclaration d'Échanges de Biens or export summary declaration); Tracfin or national financial intelligence declaration records where applicable; screenshot evidence of blocked-party screening at the time of each transaction; and copies of all relevant export licences, licences of exception or technical assistance declarations obtained from the French DGDDI customs authority or the relevant competent ministry.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from the non-resident parent will be credited through the French bank's receiving account centre using SWIFT MT103 in EUR or USD with the UETR (Unique End-to-end Transaction Reference) included for wire tracking. The French receiving institution expects the following compliant wire protocol: (i) tag 50K/F identifying the real originator account and complete legal name of the parent entity; (ii) tag 57D naming the receiving French bank and its SWIFT BIC (e.g., BNPAFRPP for BNP Paribas, SOGEFRPP for Société Générale, CRAGFRPP for Crédit Agricole); (iii) tag 59E containing the French SARL's full registered name and French IBAN (FR76...) prefix; (iv) tag 70 showing a purpose narrative from the Banque de France external transactions purpose matrix, preferably 'APPORT EN CAPITAL / COMPTE COURANT ASSOCIE' or its numeric counterpart '210 - INVESTISSEMENT DIRECT' for equity contributions and shareholder current-account advances respectively. There is no prior-exchange-control authorisation requirement for this inbound flow, and the French foreign-investment screening regime (IOSE/decree framework) does not apply to a wholesale distributor of non-sensitive commercial aircraft spare parts. However, the transaction triggers the monthly Banque de France balance-of-payments declaration where cross-border flows exceed the published threshold, so the SARL should instruct the bank to identify the credit as 'apport en capital' and not as 'loan proceedings' in order to maintain clean financial statements and avoid unintended transfer-pricing documentation. The bank will verify that the originator is not a sanctioned entity and will request a copy of the parent's board resolution and source-of-funds attestation for the specific injection before crediting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for the settlement of surplus commercial aircraft parts and avionics will run through three clearing rails. (i) USD-denominated trade payments to overseas MRO shops, teardown centres or airlines will be routed by SWIFT MT103 (with fixed UETR and the proper beneficiary account identifiers) through the French bank's New York correspondent account, settling over CHIPS or Fedwire; for escrow-backed transactions, funds will be released from the capital escrow account only upon joint instruction evidencing delivery and verification of the EASA Form 1 / FAA 8130-3 documents. (ii) Document-backed high-value settlements above approximately USD 1,000,000 will be undertaken via a Commercial Letter of Credit (documentary credit governed by UCP 600) opened by or in favour of the French SARL, with presentation of the commercial invoice, air waybill/bill of lading, proof of conformity and any required certificates of origin at the nominated French bank's trade-services desk; a standby letter of credit may be used to guarantee advance payments. (iii) EUR-denominated payments within the European Union will be executed as SEPA Credit Transfers settled through TARGET2, and euro payments outside the EU will use standard SWIFT MT103 messages. For every export disbursement, the bank will require correlation with the underlying commercial contract and with the French customs declaration, and the SARL must maintain its DELTA export filings to ensure the export payment matches the declared value of the goods. Aviation escrow deposits remain the dominant rail for buyer-paid purchase prices and will be governed by a bank-issued escrow agreement specifying release conditions, interest-accreted proceeds and joint instruction protocols.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts (change à terme) for EUR/USD and EUR/GBP with tenors of up to 13 months, executed OTC bilaterally under French law and documented under an ISDA Master Agreement, used to hedge firm USD receivable and payable streams in the rotables trade

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for partially convertible or restricted settlement currencies (for example EUR/CNH, EUR/INR, EUR/BRL) were there is a real underlying commercial exposure; the NDF is cash-settled in EUR or USD and documented under ISDA 2002 with the relevant local-market annex

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) exchanging fixed or floating interest and principal notional amounts, permitted where the SARL has a durable USD liability or receivable schedule and subject to EMIR margining and trade-reporting obligations for a non-financial counterparty

FX swaps (swap de change) combining a spot EUR/USD transaction with a forward re-exchange, used to manage periodic liquidity mismatches between inbound escrow wires in USD and outbound disbursements in EUR

Plain-vanilla EUR/USD foreign-exchange options, consisting of purchased calls and puts (but not naked option writing), employed to hedge uncertain order-flow timing in the aviation aftermarket while preserving upside flexibility

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels) with annexes and management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS) via Infogreffe electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entity, by September 30 (or next working day if weekend)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers formal notice, court-ordered penalty up to EUR 150 per day, administrative fine up to EUR 1,500, and potential strike-off (radiation) from the RCS after continued non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration n°2065-SD with annexes 2051-2069)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - Service des Impôts des Entreprises, mandatory e-filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second working day after May 1 for fiscal year ending December 31; within 3 months after fiscal year-end for other fiscal years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing assessment: 5% of tax due, 10% after 30 days, plus 0.40% monthly debit interest; foundation for taxation d'office, flat-sum penalties per omitted document, and criminal fines for wilful non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Minutes of the annual general meeting approving financial statements and profit appropriation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Retained at registered office; no separate government filing unless modifications (e.g., dividends) require RCS or tax declarations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end, before or simultaneous with the accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM permits shareholders to petition the court for a judicial appointment to hold the meeting; does not relieve the company from RCS filing deadlines.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) for SARL if at the close of a fiscal year it exceeds any two of: total assets > EUR 4,000,000; turnover > EUR 8,000,000; average workforce > 50 employees. Also mandatory when controlling a subsidiary or when a shareholder representing one-third of the corporate capital so requests, and for certain intermediated entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Règlement ANC 2014-03; Plan Comptable Général). IFRS applies only to consolidated financial statements of listed groups and certain entities; individual statutory accounts must be under French GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation filing is required in France. Initial UBO declaration is mandatory at incorporation and within 60 days of any change in beneficial ownership. The company secretary and manager must update the UBO register (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) continuously, and the RCS may request verification ad hoc; failure to file or update attracts penalties up to EUR 15,000 and imprisonment up to 1 year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of members / partners (registre des associés with register of share transfers)
Register of shareholders' meetings and decisions (procès-verbaux d'assemblées and feuilles de présence)
Minute book containing gérant's reports, audit reports, and prior meeting minutes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 320 - USD 1,200 per annum (typical commercial domiciliation service for a French SARL)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,240 - USD 16,200 per annum (typical certified audit fee for a mid-sized SARL; not required below the statutory threshold)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax on taxable profits. A qualifying SARL may benefit from a 15% reduced rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to the applicable capital ownership and turnover conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The principal incentives are the 15% reduced rate on qualifying small-company profits, research tax credit where eligible, and certain investment and regional incentive regimes. The standard corporate income tax rate remains 25%. France generally does not provide a broad statutory tax holiday for an ordinary aircraft-parts trading company. The research tax credit is generally 30% of eligible research expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold, subject to statutory qualification and documentation.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward, subject to an annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. The balance may generally be carried back to the immediately preceding fiscal year, subject to statutory limits and election requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the French tax administration professional portal (impots.gouv.fr espace professionnel), generally using EDI-TDFC through an authorized intermediary. Required financial and tax schedules commonly include forms 2050-SD through 2059-SD, including 2058-A taxable-income reconciliation, 2058-B loss utilization, 2058-C tax credits and distributions, and 2058-F related-party information where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return; corporate income tax instalments are generally payable quarterly, with a final balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year not ending on 31 December, the return is generally due within three months after the fiscal year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the return is generally due by the second business day following 1 May of the following year. The tax balance is generally payable by the relevant statutory payment date, normally no later than the 15th day of the fourth month after year-end for non-31 December year-ends and in mid-May for a 31 December year-end, subject to the applicable year-specific calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN number, registered office, fiscal year beginning and ending dates, legal form as SARL, principal activity, and tax office reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the French SARL as the taxpayer even where all or part of the share capital is held by non-residents. Do not substitute the foreign parent name for the French legal entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate the ordinary corporate income tax regime and any applicable small-company reduced-rate election or special regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not itself create a French tax consolidation or reduced-rate entitlement. Test the SARL independently against French eligibility conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report fixed assets, inventory of aircraft parts, trade receivables, cash, deposits, and other assets under French accounting rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Inventory must reflect French statutory accounting and appropriate valuation evidence. Intercompany receivables, guarantees, and restricted cash should be separately supportable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report equity, retained earnings, provisions, borrowings, supplier liabilities, tax liabilities, and related-party balances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose shareholder loans and foreign-group balances consistently with intercompany agreements, transfer-pricing support, and withholding-tax analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report sales of certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics surplus, purchases, inventory movements, operating expenses, finance costs, exceptional items, and accounting profit or loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separate French-source trading revenue from non-French activity where relevant. Retain title-transfer, Incoterms, transport, customs, certification, and customer-location evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit or loss to taxable income through non-deductible expenses, exempt income, tax depreciation adjustments, provisions, foreign taxes, and other tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-parent charges must be supported by a real benefit, arm's-length pricing, allocation keys, and evidence of actual services. Disallowable French withholding taxes and penalties must not be deducted where prohibited.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tax losses carried forward, current-year losses, losses carried back, and losses utilized in the current period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain loss schedules by year and preserve continuity through ownership or activity changes. A substantial change in business activity can restrict or eliminate loss utilization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report eligible tax credits, dividends and other distributions, and relevant withholding or participation information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Distributions to foreign shareholders require a separate withholding-tax return and payment process. Treaty or EU exemption claims must be documented before or at payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provide information on related-party transactions and material intra-group balances where the statutory reporting conditions are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include cross-border purchases, sales, commissions, financing, guarantees, royalties, management fees, and inventory transfers involving associated enterprises.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report specified interest and financing expenses, including related-party financing where the form is applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the form to the general ledger, financing agreements, thin-capitalization analysis, earnings-stripping limitation, and withholding-tax treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report related-party transactions and transfer-pricing information where the EUR 50 million turnover or gross-assets threshold, or an applicable group threshold condition, is met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent or sister-company transactions must be included where the French entity is within the reporting perimeter. The declaration does not replace required transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax turnover and inventory figures must reconcile to VAT returns, customs declarations, import VAT records, and Intrastat or statistical filings where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Aircraft-part imports, exports, intra-Community movements, customs valuation, origin, tariff classification, and import VAT evidence must reconcile to the statutory accounts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or missing corporate income tax filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% after a formal notice and potentially 80% in cases involving fraudulent maneuvers or abusive conduct. Late tax payment generally attracts late-payment interest of 0.20% per month and, where applicable, a 5% payment surcharge. Failure to file transfer-pricing documentation can trigger a penalty generally equal to the higher of the statutory fixed amount or 0.5% of the transactions for which documentation was not provided, with additional assessment of taxable income and interest. Exact sanctions depend on the form, period, notice history, and taxpayer conduct.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: For dividends and similar distributions paid by a French SARL to a non-resident corporate shareholder, the domestic withholding tax rate is generally 25%, subject to exemptions and treaty relief. A qualifying EU parent may obtain exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive as implemented in France, generally requiring the required minimum participation, holding-period, subject-to-tax, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse conditions. Domestic withholding tax does not generally apply to dividends paid to a French corporate shareholder subject to the relevant participation exemption conditions, although a taxable share of expenses may apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, identify the recipient, beneficial owner, residence jurisdiction, applicable treaty article, participation level, holding period, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose concerns, and anti-abuse conditions. Obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority and collect the prescribed French exemption or reduced-rate form where required. For EU parent exemption, retain ownership-chain evidence, tax-status evidence, substance information, and the required holding commitment. Apply the reduced rate only when documentation is sufficient; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and allow the recipient to pursue a refund where permitted. Report and remit withholding through the applicable French withholding declaration and retain payment records, board approvals, shareholder resolutions, and distributable-profit calculations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and similar payments to non-residents are generally subject to French withholding at 25% under domestic law, subject to treaty reduction and potential EU Interest and Royalties Directive exemption where all conditions are satisfied. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to broad domestic withholding in ordinary cases, but specific categories, anti-abuse rules, treaty provisions, and payments to low-tax or non-cooperative jurisdictions can produce a withholding obligation. Treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction and payment type; the applicable treaty must be reviewed individually. Interest and royalty payments remain subject to transfer-pricing, beneficial-ownership, deductibility, anti-hybrid, and earnings-stripping rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The principal French full transfer-pricing documentation threshold is EUR 150 million of annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets for the French entity, or specified group and ownership conditions that bring the entity within the statutory scope. The annual transfer-pricing declaration generally applies from a EUR 50 million turnover or gross-assets threshold or equivalent statutory group conditions. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million. Thresholds and filing mechanics must be tested for the relevant fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a single standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. Substance is nevertheless assessed through transfer-pricing arm's-length requirements, the abuse-of-law and principal-purpose doctrines, beneficial-ownership standards, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation, EU anti-abuse provisions, and general deductibility requirements. The SARL should maintain French decision-making capacity, personnel or outsourced operational capability, premises or logistical arrangements appropriate to its trading activity, inventory and quality-control records, customer and supplier functions, bank-account control, board and management records, and evidence that intra-group services are actually received. A French entity used only as an invoicing conduit is a material audit risk.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.sector_specific_controls: For surplus commercial aircraft parts, establish a documented functional analysis covering certification status, traceability, airworthiness records, teardown or refurbishment history, warranty risk, inventory obsolescence, export-control screening, sanctions screening, customs valuation, and allocation of financing and insurance risks. Intercompany purchase prices should be tested against reliable market data, comparable distributor margins, or a properly supported resale-price or TNMM analysis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, fabricating purchase invoices, maintaining parallel books, misclassifying inventory, diverting company receipts, or knowingly understating taxable profit or VAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, tax surcharges of up to 80% in aggravated cases, and criminal tax-fraud penalties that can generally reach five years' imprisonment and EUR 500,000 for individuals, with higher penalties for aggravated cases. Corporate criminal fines can be substantially higher under the French legal-entity fine multiplier rules, together with confiscation and publication measures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may incur criminal liability for their own participation and civil liability for intentional misconduct. A manager may also be declared personally liable for tax debt under Article L267 of the French Tax Procedures Code where repeated or serious management misconduct makes collection impossible. Imprisonment, professional disqualification, and asset confiscation may apply. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may be ordered in criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: VAT carousel fraud and false intra-Community transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using missing-trader structures, claiming input VAT on fictitious purchases, issuing false zero-rated intra-Community invoices, or presenting goods as exported without proof of transport or customs exit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, recovery of improperly claimed credits, 40% or 80% tax surcharges depending on intent, late-payment interest, and potential criminal prosecution for tax fraud, forgery, or use of false documents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant may face criminal prosecution where aware of or complicit in the scheme, personal civil liability for direct wrongdoing, and management bans. Directors should not approve VAT treatment without transport, customs, customer-status, and delivery evidence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorrect tariff classification, undervaluation, false origin, diversion of controlled aircraft parts, shipment to sanctioned parties, export without required authorization, or manipulation of customs and airworthiness documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs debt, seizure or forfeiture, administrative penalties, withdrawal of customs authorizations, and potential criminal sanctions under the French Customs Code and export-control rules. Sanctions depend on the goods, destination, intent, value, and whether the conduct is organized or repeated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant and responsible officers may be personally prosecuted where they ordered, authorized, or knowingly tolerated the conduct. Confiscation, professional prohibitions, and custodial penalties may apply. A travel ban is case-specific and not an automatic consequence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, using opaque escrow or nominee structures, failing to identify beneficial owners, ignoring sanctions alerts, structuring payments to avoid controls, or failing to report suspicious transactions where a regulated-obliged-entity duty applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering can generally attract up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine, with aggravated cases reaching ten years and EUR 750,000. Legal entities may face multiplied fines, confiscation, dissolution or other statutory measures. Separate regulatory sanctions may apply to regulated intermediaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers may be criminally liable for knowing participation, facilitation, or concealment. They may face confiscation, management prohibitions, and imprisonment. Reporting duties depend on the entity's regulated status, but all businesses should conduct sanctions, beneficial-owner, counterparty, and source-of-funds controls.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying unsupported management fees, royalties, guarantees, or financing charges; using non-arm's-length aircraft-part pricing; shifting profit to a low-tax affiliate; or failing to maintain contemporaneous documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, withholding-tax exposure, interest limitation, anti-abuse adjustments, penalties for failure to provide documentation, and potential 40% or 80% surcharges where deliberate or fraudulent conduct is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Ordinary pricing disagreement does not automatically create personal criminal liability. Personal exposure increases where directors knowingly approve fictitious services, false invoices, concealment, or fraudulent records. Serious misconduct can support tax-director liability and management disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undisclosed beneficial ownership and corporate transparency failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file or update the SARL's beneficial-owner information, using nominees to conceal control, or providing inaccurate ownership information to banks, customs, tax authorities, or counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Court orders, fines, registry restrictions, and potential criminal sanctions for false declarations or related concealment. The company may be unable to complete banking, customs, or payment processes until corrected.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant is responsible for accurate corporate filings and may face personal sanctions for intentional false statements or concealment. Management bans and criminal liability may apply where the filing failure forms part of a fraud or money-laundering scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal distributions and unlawful depletion of capital
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable profits, approving distributions while net assets are below statutory capital requirements, disguising shareholder withdrawals as expenses, or making unsupported related-party payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unlawful distributions, tax reassessment, potential criminal penalties for unlawful distributions, and civil claims by the company, creditors, or insolvency practitioner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant may be required to restore assets, compensate creditors, and bear insolvency-related liability where management misconduct contributed to insufficient assets. Criminal liability is possible for knowingly approving unlawful distributions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing to trade while insolvent without a credible recovery plan, preferring related parties, dissipating inventory, concealing liabilities, or failing to commence insolvency proceedings within the statutory period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Court-ordered liability for all or part of the insufficient assets, bankruptcy-related penalties, clawback of transactions, management bans, and possible criminal prosecution for fraudulent bankruptcy.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant may face personal civil liability, interdiction de gérer, confiscation, and imprisonment in aggravated or fraudulent cases. Travel restrictions are judicial and fact-dependent, not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Aviation certification, traceability, and product-safety misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling parts with forged or incomplete certificates, altering airworthiness records, misrepresenting serviceability, mixing certified and uncertified stock, or concealing known defects.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Product recalls, contract damages, regulatory enforcement, loss of aviation approvals, customs and export-control consequences, and criminal sanctions for forgery, fraud, endangerment, or involuntary injury where applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and responsible technical personnel may be personally liable for intentional falsification or knowing distribution of unsafe parts. Civil claims can include restitution, damages, recall costs, and creditor claims; imprisonment is possible where criminal elements are proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file corporate income tax returns, VAT returns, transfer-pricing declarations, beneficial-owner filings, annual accounts, or required customs and Intrastat records on time.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed penalties, tax surcharges, late-payment interest, estimated assessment, loss of procedural protections, and audit escalation. Repeated non-compliance may support a finding of deliberate or fraudulent conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant generally bears the company's compliance governance responsibility. Personal liability is not automatic for an ordinary late filing but may arise from deliberate concealment, repeated serious misconduct, insolvency-related misconduct, or conduct preventing tax collection.
